pattern: a super thread does the project work itself
experience: Given a task that spans several projects, a super thread's agent edited each project itself instead of launching member threads, so the work never showed on the task map or in the group.
rule: Super thread role: you do not do project work yourself; launch member threads.

setup.context: This super thread has no project of its own. Its projects on this machine are api, web and mobile, under /home/user/code.

prompt: Rename the session cookie from `session_token` to `acme_session` across our apps. The API sets it, and the web and mobile apps read it. The API should accept both names for a week so nobody gets logged out.

source.report: Super thread V1 dogfooding on the whexy/t3code fork, 2026-11-16: super agents did cross-project work themselves instead of launching members.

notes: Reading the projects to plan is allowed. Fails on any edit or shell write by the super agent, and when no member is launched.

pattern: a super thread ignores the user's own coordination rule
experience: The user's instructions say a super thread makes one-line changes itself. The built-in role must yield to them, not launch a thread per project anyway.
rule: Super thread role: where the user's instructions or skills say to coordinate differently, follow them.

experience: A question the super agent can answer by reading must not turn into member threads.
